decision: bounded read-only status reconciliation after ambiguous synthetic workload stop

reviews.correctness: A stop transport failure is ambiguous: the worker may already have persisted stopped state. Re-sending start is unsafe; status must prove a terminal state. The end-to-end calibration gate must distinguish a lost response after durable stop from a stop that never committed.
reviews.robustness_security: Use only the existing bounded qrexec service with a read-only status action. Never signal recorded PIDs and never weaken duration bounds. Fail closed if terminal state cannot be proven after bounded probes.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Fast path adds zero calls when stop returns stopped/not-running/completed. Failure path adds at most 3 read-only probes with bounded delay; no daemon, database, listener, MissionQueue change, or extra call on successful cleanup.

alternatives.name: trust stop attempt
alternatives.rejected: cannot prove remote cleanup after timeout or lost response

alternatives.name: repeat stop only
alternatives.rejected: idempotent but still cannot distinguish repeated transport loss from confirmed cleanup

alternatives.name: persistent workload-control daemon
alternatives.rejected: adds lifecycle, memory, credential and attack-surface cost before Qubes qualification

qa: status is read-only and reports running/stopped/not-running
acknowledged terminal stop uses no extra probe
end-to-end calibration simulates stop committed remotely but response lost, then requires status confirmation and a stopped worker state
end-to-end calibration also simulates stop failing before commit and requires three bounded status probes followed by fail-closed rejection
partial start rollback reports both start failure and unresolved cleanup
collector still accepts reconciled calibration evidence only when provenance and workload bindings are valid

comparison_result.winner: positive terminal-state reconciliation through read-only status
comparison_result.correctness: distinguishes committed cleanup with lost response from cleanup that never committed
comparison_result.robustness: keeps failure ambiguous until terminal state is positively observed
comparison_result.latency: zero overhead on normal stops; bounded retry latency only on ambiguous stops
comparison_result.resource_use: constant small probe overhead and no persistent service
comparison_result.regression_risk: test/evidence expansion only in this step; production stop semantics remain unchanged

failure_lessons: A transport exception is not proof that the remote stop failed.
An attempted stop is not equivalent to confirmed remote cleanup.
Integration QA must model both sides of the ambiguity: response lost after commit and failure before commit.
